Wyszogrod Old Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Wyszogród, Poland

Demolished. Jews lived in Wyszogród from at least the 1420s, though the community wasn't formally independent until 1753; sources disagree whether this cemetery dates to the 15th, 16th, or 17th century. It served Jews from Wyszogród and neighboring towns until overcrowding, worsened by an 1831 cholera epidemic, prompted the founding of a newer cemetery. Under Communist rule, a fruit and vegetable processing plant was built directly on the site; a 1963 landslide collapsed part of the slope it sat on. Archaeological excavations in 1971 and 1973 uncovered 49 graves, but found no matzevot or tombstone traces. By 1921 the town's Jewish population had reached 2,465; most were deported via Czerwińsk and Nowy Dwór Mazowiecki to Auschwitz-Birkenau in 1941-1942.
